drg.description: Kidney and Urinary Tract Infections without MCC

notes.text:
HISTORY AND PHYSICAL. Chart, labs and overnight events reviewed. 65-year-old female admitted for urinary tract infection. Admission data:
Day 0: labs bilirubin 0.68, creatinine 1.86, hemoglobin 13-13.1, platelets 282-293, sodium 139-140, wbc 7.7-8.1; vitals dbp 75-79, heart_rate 79-83, map 89-93, o2_flow 0, resp_rate 16-17, sbp 116-120, spo2 97-98, temp 36.7-36.9
Day 0 orders/meds/results: Urinalysis: positive nitrites, >50 WBC/hpf; Ceftriaxone 1 g IV
Assessment and plan: Urinary tract infection. Chronic kidney disease stage 3. Acute kidney injury ruled out.

PROGRESS NOTE, hospital day 1. Patient seen and examined at bedside. Data:
Day 1: labs creatinine 1.89-1.91, hemoglobin 13, platelets 282-290, sodium 139, wbc 7.5-8; vitals dbp 77-80, heart_rate 79-84, map 91-94, o2_flow 0, resp_rate 16-17, sbp 116-122, spo2 98, temp 36.7-36.9
Day 1 orders/meds/results: Ceftriaxone 1 g IV
Assessment and plan: Urinary tract infection. Chronic kidney disease stage 3. Acute kidney injury ruled out. Continue current management.

DISCHARGE SUMMARY. 65-year-old female, length of stay 3 days. Hospital course: treated per the plan above with daily labs and vital signs; stable for discharge. Medications reconciled and return precautions reviewed. Discharge diagnoses: Urinary tract infection. Chronic kidney disease stage 3. Acute kidney injury ruled out. Follow up with primary care in one week. Patient seen and examined at bedside.
